chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Eat from the birds that have a beak and no claws." He was asked about water birds, and he said the same.

key_terms.طَيْرُ الْمَاءِ: Water birds, such as ducks or geese.
key_terms.قَانِصَةٌ: A beak or bill, specifically referring to the hard covering of a bird's mouth.
key_terms.مِخْلَبَ: Claws or talons, typically found on birds of prey.

ai.seo_question: What are the physical characteristics that make a bird halal to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the criterion of possessing a beak (qanisah) and lacking talons (mikhlab) to distinguish permissible birds from predatory ones, a ruling extended to water birds to ensure clarity in dietary laws. This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on observable physical traits to determine halal status, aligning with the broader Islamic principle of consuming clean and non-predatory creatures.
